newsitem.title: CHINA: JILIN SAYS NO ASSET INJECTION PLANNED.
newsitem.headline: JILIN SAYS NO ASSET INJECTION PLANNED.

text.p: Jilin Chemical Industrial Co Ltd said on Friday its ultimate parents will examine and consider corporation restructurings but Jilin Chemical currently has no plan to restructure or take new operations from them.

"Jilin Chemical currently does not have a restructuring plan and has received no information from (ultimate parents) the Ministry of Chemical Industries or Jilin province relating to restructuring plans," Lu Qirong told a news briefing.
But the province and the ministry will examine and consider possible restructurings of state-owned enterprises under their supervision, he said.

Hong Kong-listed Jilin Chemical is a subsidiary of Jilin Chemical Group Corp, controlled by the Jilin provincial government and under the industrial supervision of China's Ministry of Chemical Industries.
Speculation of a restructuring in which Ministry of Chemical Industries would inject good assets and operations into Jilin Chemical had boosted the stock, brokers said.
Shares of Jilin Cheimical surged more than 100 percent in the past month to close at HK$2.10 on Friday from HK$1.04 on July 9.
But Lu added that the mainland government was speeding up reform of large and medium-sized state-owned enterprises.
"The state recently held a meeting with 120 enterprises to study and discuss how to develop holding companies," he said.

Since China's state-owned companies were still small, compared to their counterparts overseas, it was natural to consider grouping different enterprises from a particular industry in one entity, Lu added.
"Every province and ministry will consider this issue, and I believe Jilin province and the Ministry of Chemical Industries will be no exception," he said.
However, Jilin Chemical was well placed to expand its assets since it had an option to purchase seven ethylene plants from its parent anytime in five years after the plants were completed, Lu said.

The company planned to issue 300 million A-shares for China's domestic investors over the next 12 months and the proceeds could be used to fund the purchase, he said, giving no details of the timing of such a purchase, which could total more than 120 million yuan. -- Hong Kong newsroom (852) 2843 6369
